publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Interaction between microbiota and immunity in health and disease

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the two-way traffic between the commensal microbiota and the mammalian immune system - how microbes train immunity and how immunity in turn shapes which microbes persist
span.quote: Here, we review features of microbiome-immunity crosstalk and their roles in health and disease, while providing examples of molecular mechanisms orchestrating these interactions in the intestine and extra-intestinal organs. We highlight aspects of the current knowledge, challenges and limitations in achieving causal understanding of host immune-microbiome interactions, as well as their impact on immune-mediated diseases, and discuss how these insights may translate towards future development of microbiometargeted therapeutic interventions.

span.label: which microbiome-immunity interactions are mechanistically established, and what still stands between association and a causal claim in human disease
span.quote: Indeed, current evidence from animal models indicates a bidirectional relationship to exist between microbiome perturbation and immune dysregulation. As such, distinct microbiota and metabolites drive immune activation, and chronic in flammation conversely may shape the dysbiotic con figuration and functions of microbial communities. However, a direct causal relationship between the microbiome and immunity before the onset or during early stages of disease has not been established in most medical conditions.

span.label: a review that organises the mechanisms by compartment and by disease and then states plainly that a direct causal relationship has not been established in most medical conditions - the negative claim is the contribution
span.quote: More importantly, the causal effect of the microbiome on immune dysregulation in most human disorders listed above remains to be proven.

span.label: critique
span.quote: Here, we review features of microbiome-immunity crosstalk and their roles in health and disease, while providing examples of molecular mechanisms orchestrating these interactions in the intestine and extra-intestinal organs. We highlight aspects of the current knowledge, challenges and limitations in achieving causal understanding of host immune-microbiome interactions, as well as their impact on immune-mediated diseases, and discuss how these insights may translate towards future development of microbiometargeted therapeutic interventions.

span.label: host-microbe mutualism and its breakdown - a relationship in which each side regulates the other, so that neither perturbation nor dysregulation can be read as the cause of the other from observation alone
span.quote: Indeed, current evidence from animal models indicates a bidirectional relationship to exist between microbiome perturbation and immune dysregulation. As such, distinct microbiota and metabolites drive immune activation, and chronic in flammation conversely may shape the dysbiotic con figuration and functions of microbial communities. However, a direct causal relationship between the microbiome and immunity before the onset or during early stages of disease has not been established in most medical conditions.

span.label: a narrative review of germ-free, gnotobiotic, antibiotic-depletion and dietary animal work alongside human association studies, with the review's own scope limits stated - it refers out to other reviews rather than claiming coverage
span.term: a narrative review of germ-free, gnotobiotic, antibiotic-depletion and dietary animal work alongside human association studies, with the review's own scope limits stated - it refers out to other reviews rather than claiming coverage
span.quote: As the large body of evidence related to host immune-microbiome interactions cannot be summarized by a single review, we aim to provide key concepts and examples of such interactions and their potential effects on human health and disease risk, while referring throughout the review to multiple other recent reviews 14–16 focusing on distinct aspects of these emerging interactions.

span.label: the causal claims of this field rest on germ-free animals - raised with no commensals at all. That is the cleanest possible contrast and it is also a state no animal is ever in outside a facility, so what it establishes is that commensals matter, not which ones do what at natural abundance
span.term: an instrument that is an extreme, not a control
span.quote: The study of mechanistic causal relationships between commensal microbiota and host immunity is strongly informed by the use of germ-free (GF) animal models. Early studies on GF animals demonstrated that absence of commensal microbes is associated with profound intestinal defects of lymphoid tissue architecture and immune functions.

span.label: microbiota drive immune activation and inflammation conversely reshapes the microbial community. When each side changes the other, an observed association in a diseased human carries no direction, which is exactly why the authors say the causal relationship before onset has not been established
span.quote: Indeed, current evidence from animal models indicates a bidirectional relationship to exist between microbiome perturbation and immune dysregulation. As such, distinct microbiota and metabolites drive immune activation, and chronic in flammation conversely may shape the dysbiotic con figuration and functions of microbial communities. However, a direct causal relationship between the microbiome and immunity before the onset or during early stages of disease has not been established in most medical conditions.

span.label: 16S rRNA sequencing reports genus and composition. Every strain-level and every functional difference in the reviewed literature was therefore not measured rather than not present - and the recommendation to move to shotgun metagenomics is a statement about what the existing corpus of findings could not have seen
span.quote: In addition, many studies focusing on microbiome-immunity interaction have utilized 16S rRNA sequencing to characterize the microbiome, but this modality is limited by its genus-level and purely compositional resolution. Given that strain level resolution and functional insights are better served by shotgun metagenomic sequencing, the field is expected to increasingly rely on this more sophisticated methodology (in addition to metatranscriptomics, metabolomics, metaproteomics and culturomics) in decoding immune-microbiota interactions.

span.label: NLRP6's effect on microbiota structure appears only where the background microbiota contains particular pathobionts such as Helicobacter. A knockout phenotype that depends on the vivarium is a joint property of gene and facility, and two labs reporting different results may both be right
span.term: the phenotype belongs partly to the building
span.quote: Importantly, the impact of NLRP6 on microbiota community structure is dependent on the background microbiota in the vivarium, with dysbiosis occurring in mice lacking NLRP6 only in the presence of distinct microbiome configuration containing pathobionts such as Helicobacter spp

span.label: faecal microbiome transplantation aims to restore a healthy microbiome configuration, and the authors state there is no general consensus on which features constitute a healthy microbiome. The therapy is specified by its mechanism and not by its endpoint
span.quote: For example, in an aim to restore a healthy microbiome configuration in patients suffering from dysbiosis linked to immune-mediated disease, fecal microbiome transplantation (FMT), which has so far been widely used in Clostridium dif ficile infections, is considered also as potential treatment in this clinical context. However, there is still no general consensus on which features constitute a ‘healthy’ microbiome. The ef ficacy of FMT in diseases such as IBD, is therefore still under evaluation and many challenges remain to be overcome, including optimization of fecal processing and patient safety.

span.label: a direct causal relationship between the microbiome and immunity before onset or in early disease has not been established in most medical conditions
span.quote: Indeed, current evidence from animal models indicates a bidirectional relationship to exist between microbiome perturbation and immune dysregulation. As such, distinct microbiota and metabolites drive immune activation, and chronic in flammation conversely may shape the dysbiotic con figuration and functions of microbial communities. However, a direct causal relationship between the microbiome and immunity before the onset or during early stages of disease has not been established in most medical conditions.

span.label: the causal effect of the microbiome on immune dysregulation in most human disorders remains to be proven
span.quote: More importantly, the causal effect of the microbiome on immune dysregulation in most human disorders listed above remains to be proven.

span.label: the field runs on laboratory mice whose microbiota is divergent from wild animals and humans, limiting translational potential and reproducibility
span.quote: Importantly in all of these efforts, the microbiome research community massively uses laboratory mice that harbor a divergent microbiota from ‘wild’ animals and humans, thereby featuring a limited translational potential and reproducibility as compared to ‘real-life’ settings.

span.label: most of the reviewed work used 16S rRNA sequencing, which resolves genus and composition only and cannot see strain-level or functional differences
span.quote: In addition, many studies focusing on microbiome-immunity interaction have utilized 16S rRNA sequencing to characterize the microbiome, but this modality is limited by its genus-level and purely compositional resolution. Given that strain level resolution and functional insights are better served by shotgun metagenomic sequencing, the field is expected to increasingly rely on this more sophisticated methodology (in addition to metatranscriptomics, metabolomics, metaproteomics and culturomics) in decoding immune-microbiota interactions.

span.label: inter-individual variation typically explains more variance in both microbiome and immune response than disease state does
span.quote: Finally, the microbiome configuration and immune responses are both increasingly appreciated to be highly variable among human individuals, with more variances typically explained by inter-individual variation than by disease state.

span.label: there is no general consensus on which features constitute a healthy microbiome, so FMT efficacy in IBD remains under evaluation
span.quote: For example, in an aim to restore a healthy microbiome configuration in patients suffering from dysbiosis linked to immune-mediated disease, fecal microbiome transplantation (FMT), which has so far been widely used in Clostridium dif ficile infections, is considered also as potential treatment in this clinical context. span.label: the prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy of traditional individual probiotics in promoting human health is limited

span.label: microbiome depletion by broad-spectrum antibiotics in humans, followed by seasonal influenza vaccination and plasma metabolome profiling

span.quote: In humans with pre-existing immune system impairment, microbiome depletion through broad-spectrum antibiotics not only results in a diminished antibody response to seasonal in fluenza vaccination, but also leads to augmented circulatory in flammatory signatures and altered plasma metabolome pro files.

span.label: a modality limited to genus-level and purely compositional resolution, as against shotgun metagenomics which resolves strain and function
span.quote: In addition, many studies focusing on microbiome-immunity interaction have utilized 16S rRNA sequencing to characterize the microbiome, but this modality is limited by its genus-level and purely compositional resolution. Given that strain level resolution and functional insights are better served by shotgun metagenomic sequencing, the field is expected to increasingly rely on this more sophisticated methodology (in addition to metatranscriptomics, metabolomics, metaproteomics and culturomics) in decoding immune-microbiota interactions.

span.quote: Finally, the microbiome configuration and immune responses are both increasingly appreciated to be highly variable among human individuals, with more variances typically explained by inter-individual variation than by disease state.
